_readme: Ramya's own authoritative professional profile. This file is the ONLY source opportunity_scoring.py and resume_tailoring.py may cite as fact. verified_experience is the only category resume_tailoring.py may present as fact in a draft. transferable_experience and knowledge_training may inform ramya_fit.gaps and framing language but are never rendered as hands-on fact. claims_requiring_verification are never used in any draft until moved to verified_experience by hand. This first populated version was drafted by Claude from (a) real, founder-published content already live on aiforui.org (the About page, and sales-director/runtime/config/practitioner-bank.json, both reviewed and approved before this task) and (b) facts stated directly by Ramya in the profile-population request, per AOS-PRACTICE-VALIDATION-ROADMAP.md's evidence discipline. Anything named in the request but not found in existing published material was classified CLAIM_REQUIRES_VERIFICATION rather than VERIFIED, per the request's own instruction: 'if any fact cannot be confidently supported by existing authoritative material, leave it out or classify it as CLAIM_REQUIRES_VERIFICATION.' This is a DRAFT pending Ramya's own review before it is treated as canonical (see opportunity-intelligence-model.md's 'profile is read-only, founder-authoritative' rule) — nothing in Opportunity Intelligence has written or will write to this file; it is edited by hand only.

schema.verified_experience: array of {id, category, claim, employer_or_context, dates, tags, evidence_note} — category is one of: role, certification, project, skill, achievement. tags drive opportunity_scoring.py's tag-overlap matching. This is the only category resume_tailoring.py may present as fact.
schema.transferable_experience: array of {id, category, claim, context, dates, tags, evidence_note} — real experience in an adjacent area that supports but does not prove a specific target-domain claim; contributes to a fit score at a discounted (0.4x) weight, never as strong as a verified match
schema.knowledge_training: array of {id, category, claim, source, dates, tags, evidence_note} — training, certifications, frameworks studied, or self-study; tags are still recorded for gap-analysis visibility, but knowledge_training never contributes to an employment fit score (only verified_matches/transferable_matches do) — this is what keeps a certification from silently becoming an implementation claim
schema.claims_requiring_verification: array of {id, category, claim, note} — named in the profile-population request but not found in any existing authoritative material; excluded from every draft and from every score until Ramya confirms it and moves it to verified_experience by hand
schema.target_professional_areas: array of strings — roles/domains Ramya is targeting, not a claim of experience in them. Descriptive only; not yet consumed by any scoring code.
schema.engagement_preferences: array of strings — format/geography/industry preferences, not qualifications. Descriptive only; not yet consumed by any scoring code.
schema.guardrails: array of strings — standing rules for anyone (human or future code) editing or extending this file. Not data to be matched against; a permanent reminder embedded in the file itself.

verified_experience.claim: Holds NIST AI RMF, CAISR, EU GDPR Practitioner, and Microsoft AI Transformation Leader certifications.
verified_experience.evidence_note: Verbatim from aiforui.org About page and practitioner-bank.json's 'certifications' entry. Deliberately tagged with 'certification' only, no domain tags (e.g. 'ai governance') — holding a certification is a verified fact, but per the profile-population request's own explicit rule, a certification must never by itself inflate a fit score toward hands-on AI governance implementation. The knowledge these certifications represent is captured separately under knowledge_training, which does not contribute to a fit score.

transferable_experience.claim: Risk/control framework design, gap-analysis methodology, and governance-programme delivery built over 13+ years of GRC/technology risk/TPRM work is directly relevant to AI governance control design and AI risk-framework operationalization — but hands-on delivery of an AI-specific governance implementation is not yet established.

transferable_experience.evidence_note: A reasoned characterization, not a documented fact — this is exactly what 'transferable' means: real, verified underlying skill (see thirteen-years-grc-experience, pwc-control-testing-residual-risk), applied to a target domain where implementation itself isn't yet evidenced. Contributes to a fit score only at the 0.4x discounted weight opportunity_scoring.py applies to transferable matches.
